notes.decision: Translated 'her lash/affliction' tentatively. ⲉⲥⲓϣ likely = ⲉⲥⲏϣ 'blow, lash, stripe' with feminine possessive ⲡⲉⲥ-. The feminine antecedent is uncertain (perhaps Hyle or the kingdom of darkness from prior page). ⲁⲓ̈ⲧ following the gap reads as a qualitative ending (-ⲁⲓⲧ pattern: ⲇⲣⲁⲓⲧ, ⲧⲁⲭⲁⲓⲧ); the gap likely held the verbal stem.

Read as Lyc. ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise up' (per terminology guide; preserves vertical semantics). With ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ 'in shame' = 'raised up (exposed) in shame' — describing the punitive exhibition of the bound powers.

Translated 'principalities/leaders.' Lexeme of unclear etymology, possibly related to ⲝⲱⲣⲉ 'mighty' (= ϫⲱⲣⲉ) with prefix, or a Manichaean technical term for an archonic class. Recurs in lines 26-27 ('all the principalities of the kingship'), confirming a class of cosmic powers. Flagged for parallels.

Read as Lyc. perfect 'those whom they bound' from a verb ⲕⲁⲧϩ (possibly = ⲕⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'gather, bind' or ⲕⲱⲧϣ̄ 'turn, twist'). Context (in sequence with 'gathered them in,' 'fixed in the wheel,' 'bound them') confirms a binding/capturing sense.
Translated 'they reckoned them' from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (per accumulated vocab). The Lyc. form ⲟⲁⲡ shows vocalic doubling.

Translated 'in single accord' from ⲧⲱⲧ 'agreement, joining' (Lyc. ⲧⲟⲁⲧ). Could alternatively be 'in single grasp' if ⲧⲟⲁⲧ = ⲧⲱⲧ 'hand,' but the agreement-sense fits the cosmological binding image better.
ϣⲏϣ = 'be equal' (Sah. ϣⲏϣ); ⲛⲉⲙⲉⲩ = 'with them.' The clause indicates the Enmity-powers are equal/proportionate to their punishment-instrument.

Read as Lyc. variant of ⲛⲉⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'they were there' (locative) — 'they were abiding there.' Alternative reading: ⲙⲏⲛ qualitative 'remaining.' Either yields 'they were (there) at the place where they stand fast in him.'

Translated 'upon the whole tree' reading ⲡϣⲉ as 'wood/tree' (ϣⲉ). Pairs with ⲡⲕⲁⲍ 'earth' as the dual destination of fallen matter cast back from the wheel. Could alternatively be 'the whole field' (ⲥⲱϣⲉ) or 'the whole abyss/depth' (ϣⲏ). Sense uncertain.

Translated 'they reigned to seize.' ⲁⲩⲣⲣⲟ = perfect 'they became kings/reigned'; ⲉϩⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ = ⲉ + ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'in order to grasp/seize.' The bound powers in the wheel are likened to those who once reigned by usurping kingship.

Translated 'multitude' (= ⲙⲏⲏϣⲉ) — interpreting the doubled-ⲟ as a Lyc. orthographic feature. Alternative 'midst' (ⲙⲏⲧⲉ) is also possible. The phrase 'in the multitude of mighty Aeons' fits the cosmological image of seizing kingship amid abundant powers.

Compound ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲝⲁⲓ- ('love' or 'boast') + ⲙ̄ⲗⲁⲍ ('strife,' per accumulated ⲙⲗⲟⲟϩ/ⲙ̄ⲗⲁϩ). Translated 'love-of-strife' = warlike contention. Listed alongside 'desire of women' and 'multitude of property' as constitutive vices of the bound archons.

Translated 'his hunger' reading ⲡⲉϩ- as Lyc. possessive 'his' (per accumulated vocab) + ϩⲕⲟ 'hunger.' Antecedent of 'his' is lost in the preceding lacunae but likely references one of the bound archonic powers whose hunger drove forth the animals.
